name: Process stage ladder
reader_question: How far has a measure progressed through its ordered process, and when was each stage reached?
relationship: Ordered stages of one process as rising steps; each shows the date reached or is hollow and dashed when not yet reached.
use_when: A single measure moves through a fixed order of stages (proposal, consultation, adoption, entry into force, implementation)
The reader needs to see which stages have and have not been reached
avoid_when: Stages can be reached out of order or skipped — use evidence-milestone-strip or a table
Several measures are compared — use duration-bars or a status matrix

data_contract.notes: Date at which reached / not-yet-reached is read
Date reached; null = not yet reached. Reached dates ascend and do not follow asOf

units: Ordinal stages; dates are labels, not positions.

editable: Steps and text as native shapes and text boxes
not_data_bound: Step heights encode order only, not elapsed time; they are positioned from the fixture at build time and are not data-bound

table_alternative: A stage table (stage, status, date reached) for exact dates and sources.
variations: Ladder with a distinct date for announcement versus effective date inside one stage
Vertical ladder for long stage names
limitations: Equal step widths do not represent elapsed time between stages; use duration-bars for that
A stage without a date is treated as not reached, never as skipped

excluded_alternatives.reason: Stages are not equal-effort units, so a percentage would be a synthetic score
Implies attrition of quantities between stages, which a single measure does not have
